sources.content: # jemberlow/authgate. Jemberlow Authgate is a sign-in proxy that sits in front of internal web apps and checks each request for a valid session. The image is built on `debian:12-slim` and runs as the non-root user `gate` with UID 10001. It listens on port 4180 for HTTP and serves Prometheus metrics on port 9180 at `/metrics`. The entrypoint is `/usr/local/bin/authgate serve`. Session data is kept in memory unless `AUTHGATE_REDIS_URL` is set.

Configuration. `AUTHGATE_UPSTREAM` (required, no default) is the URL of the app being protected. `AUTHGATE_COOKIE_NAME` defaults to `_authgate`, and `AUTHGATE_SESSION_TTL` defaults to `8h`. `AUTHGATE_ALLOWED_DOMAINS` limits sign-in to the listed email domains and defaults to empty, which allows none. Mount a volume at `/etc/authgate` to supply `providers.yaml`. The health check calls `GET /ping` every 30 seconds and marks the container unhealthy after 3 failures. `AUTHGATE_LOG_LEVEL` defaults to `info`. Set `AUTHGATE_COOKIE_SECURE` to `false` only for local testing over plain HTTP.

claims.text: Jemberlow Authgate runs as the non-root user gate with UID 10001.
The default Jemberlow Authgate session lifetime is 24 hours.
Jemberlow Authgate reads providers.yaml from a volume mounted at /etc/authgate.
Jemberlow Authgate serves Prometheus metrics on port 9180.
Jemberlow Authgate keeps session data in memory unless AUTHGATE_REDIS_URL is set.
